FOR campaign/underworld-peoples -- TWO FAILURES, ONE MECHANICAL AND ONE WORTH A THOUGHT. 74adac6eb944, gate rc=2 at 354.4s.

1. the_reckoning_renders_the_epoch_pair -- MECHANICAL.

   The expected list predates your four peoples; the live render has Fovfav
   (duergars), Wodbog (kuo toas), Dazhaf (mountain dwarfs) and Kxsonkxzo
   (svirfneblins) in it. Refresh the list.

   Do not stop at the list, though: the assertion's own message still says
   "ten organized priesthoods of FIFTEEN placed peoples", and there are
   nineteen now. That sentence is the kind of prose that goes stale beside a
   refreshed fixture and then misinforms the next reader -- this repo has a
   named habit of it (hand-authored prose beside generated blocks). Update
   both in the same commit.

2. exposure_sound_reports_false_when_the_toponymic_gates_are_removed -- READ
   THIS ONE BEFORE FIXING IT.

     "seed 7 goblins must root these toponymic concepts for this test to bite"
     live   ["river", "ford", "marsh", "spring"]
     wanted ["river", "ford", "valley", "marsh", "spring"]

   Seed 7's goblins stopped rooting `valley`. That is an ANTI-VACUITY guard
   telling you its subject moved, not a list to trim.

   MY HYPOTHESIS, WHICH IS YOURS TO CONFIRM OR KILL: a lexicon entry is a Root
   or a Gap depending on EXPOSURE -- whether that people is placed somewhere
   the concept applies. You added four peoples, which changes competition for
   sites, which moves placement, which moves biome exposure. Goblins losing
   `valley` on seed 7 would be a downstream consequence of your peoples being
   placed at all, not of anything you did to the lexicon. If so it is expected
   and interesting: adding underworld peoples reshapes where SURFACE peoples
   end up.

   I have not verified that chain. What would settle it: compare goblin
   placement on seed 7 between main and your branch. If they moved, the story
   holds; if they did not, something changed exposure directly and that is a
   different and more surprising finding.

   ON THE FIX: this guard needs SOME toponymic concepts rooted to be able to
   bite, and four may serve as well as five. But pinning a five-element list
   means every campaign that moves placement re-pins it -- and you are the
   second tonight to hit a guard of exactly that shape. The durable version
   derives the set: take the toponymic concepts this people actually roots,
   assert the set is non-empty (or has at least N members), and proceed. That
   keeps the anti-vacuity property and stops the list being a snapshot.
   campaign/the-seedbed did precisely this a few hours ago with
   `measured_text_of` and it is worth a look as a worked example.
